Text at the top reads: I got the grain bin open in nine minutes. Everyone wants to know where the grain went. Nobody's impressed by my progress.
posts.caption: I found the feed room door standing open at 6:15 and I knew before I looked. Pudding was in the aisle with oats on his nose and the calm face of someone who has nothing to explain. Three scoops were gone, which in pony terms is a banquet. I swept for twenty minutes and spent the rest of the morning wondering who taught him. He watched the broom the whole time. That afternoon I bought a carabiner for the bin lid. The man at the feed store said it won't help. I bought two.
posts.first: My first pony taught me to check every lid and latch twice. I still do it every night with a flashlight, in my slippers, like someone guarding a vault. Pudding watches from his stall and doesn't say a word. I think he's taking notes.

posts.caption: The new blankets came in on Tuesday, tags still on, and I put the biggest one on my draft mare before a morning of rain. By ten the paddock was a soup of brown water and the herd was lined up under the roof like commuters. All except one mare, who stood in the middle of it with her blanket soaked to the girth. She had the look of someone who'd read the tag and chosen to test it. I toweled her for half an hour. She leaned into every minute.
posts.first: I own a rain jacket with a hole in the left elbow that I've been meaning to replace since 2019. It hangs by the barn door and has met every storm with me. Last week my husband offered to buy a new one. I told him this one still works. He said it doesn't. It's still on the hook.

posts.quote: My neighbor asked what I do with a horse all day. I told her the truth: I carry water, and I'm supervised.
posts.first: Last Saturday I hauled forty gallons of water, three bales, and one very opinionated wheelbarrow across the yard before nine. The horse watched from the shade and flicked an ear when I dropped a bucket. I took it as encouragement. My neighbor waved from her porch with a coffee.

posts.caption: Our tack room has a coffee can on the shelf. It isn't for coffee. It's where the dentist money goes when the hay guy raises his price, and it has been getting lighter since August. I counted it on Sunday and found a note in my own handwriting that said 'blanket first.' I have no memory of writing it. I looked over the stall door at my round bay mare asleep under a lavender cooler with a cat on her back, and I understood myself completely. The dentist can wait another winter.
posts.first: The barn cat picked her spot on that mare's back in October and hasn't moved since, except for meals. I tiptoe in at night to check the water and neither of them opens an eye. It's the best-run operation on the property, and it costs me two bags of kibble a month.

posts.caption: The new gelding showed up in September with a trailer full of opinions. He tried the gate, the water trough, and the fence charger before lunch on his first day. The old gray in the end stall watched all of it from under his forelock and said nothing. Two weeks later the new one was standing beside him every afternoon, chewing at exactly the same speed. I don't know what was said. The quiet in that barn has gotten noticeably better, and the gate hasn't been touched since.
posts.first: My husband says that horse has the best posture in the county for his age. I tell him it's the bifocals. They make him look like he's reading something important. He's mostly checking who is holding a carrot. He has been right every single time.

posts.caption: The vet's invoice came in an envelope heavier than I wanted. Inside was a number with a comma in it and a line that said 'dental float.' I stood in the kitchen reading it twice, then walked out to the barn in my socks. She was at the stall door with her forelock perfectly arranged, which is her way of saying everything is fine. I scratched under her halter and said nothing. The check went out Friday. The forelock stayed arranged all week.
posts.first: My mother used to say you don't buy a horse, you sign up for a second mortgage with feelings. I laughed at the time. I've since had a conversation with my own bank. They were polite. The horse was not present for that meeting.
